`case_study:booking-priceline-2002-2025` · tickers US-BKNG · confidence: verified

Priceline fell from ~$974 (1999, adjusted for the 2003 1:6 reverse split) to ~$6.60-7 in Oct 2002 (-99%). CEO Jeffery Boyd and team bought UK Active Hotels (2004) and Dutch Booking.com (2005, ~$133m [unverified]); Booking.com's agency model (hotels pay commission after stay, broad SME hotel supply in Europe) became the profit engine. Fortune (2017): best total shareholder return of any large company over the prior decade; ~3,000% in 10 years to 2015. Reached ~$1,500+ by 2016-17 and ~$5,000-5,800 by 2025 [unverified]: roughly 800x from the 2002 low. Split: mostly EPS growth (gross bookings compounding 20-30% for a decade plus margin expansion and buybacks); P/E stayed ~20-30x [unverified]. Drawdowns: -99% 2000-02; ~-70% 2008 [unverified]; ~-45% 2020 COVID. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2005-07: international gross bookings growing far faster than the US name-your-own-price business and becoming the majority of profit, disclosed in segment data — while the market still saw a damaged US dot-com. Who caught it: few documented names; it was a classic 'hidden segment' that analysts initially underweighted. Stall: post-2018 growth normalised to ~10%, still compounding via buybacks. LESSON: a small acquired segment with platform economics inside an unloved parent can carry the whole valuation; read the segment notes.

- **Start → end:** ~$6.60 (Oct 2002, reverse-split adj) → ~$5,000-5,800 (2025) [unverified] (~800x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly EPS + buybacks
- **Max drawdown:** -99% (2000-02); ~-70% 2008 [unverified]
- **Early signal:** Booking.com/Active Hotels international bookings growth in segment data
- **Who caught it:** not well documented
- **Ended/stalled:** growth normalised post-2018; still compounding
- **Lesson:** hidden segment with platform economics inside a broken parent
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.fool.com/investing/2017/09/18/could-the-priceline-group-inc-be-a-millionaire-mak.aspx) · [2](https://fortune.com/2014/02/06/booking-returns-on-priceline/) · [3](https://money.cnn.com/2015/08/05/investing/priceline-earnings-stock) · [4](https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/priceline-stock-history-how-the-internet-travel-giant-became-a-blockbuster-stock)

`insight:flag-cash-pile-context` · verified

RULE: cash is the easiest number to forge, so test that it behaves like cash. (1) YIELD: interest/other income divided by average cash + liquid investments should be near prevailing deposit/T-bill rates (India FDs ~6-8% in most years; US T-bills 0-5%). Satyam's ~Rs 5,000 cr+ 'cash' produced too little real interest; Rs 376 cr of accrued interest was fake. Adjust for mark-to-market funds where gains sit in other income or OCI, and for cash held near year-end only. (2) LOCATION: cash in the company's own name at named banks vs 'trustee', escrow or offshore-subsidiary accounts (Wirecard EUR 1.9 bn in Philippine trustee accounts; Cox & Kings foreign subsidiaries). (3) BEHAVIOUR: holding large cash while also borrowing is irrational unless the cash is trapped, restricted or fake (CLSA on Satyam, Sep 2008: ~$1.2 bn cash yet $56 m of debt). Cash that never returns to shareholders, never funds visible capex and keeps growing with reported profit (not CFO) is a flag. (4) CONSISTENCY: change in cash should reconcile with CFO - capex - dividends. BENIGN WHEN: yield matches market rates, cash is in named banks/AAA instruments, the company returns cash or uses it visibly (Info Edge's large investment book is disclosed by investee and marked to listed prices). TEST: compute yield each year; read the cash note for restricted balances and banks; check gross debt alongside cash.

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:NAVINFLUOR:chemours-plant-commissioned-q3fy27`
- **Method:** promise-tracker credibility · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.60 · resolve by 2027-02-28
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (30-Oct-2026): 'The Chemours project… is also progressing towards commissioning in Q3 FY27.' Analyst notes 'we've seen some delay'; MD Anish Ganatra calls the delay 'a conscious choice' over process route. Other promises in the same call: R32/HFC expansion 'on track for commissioning shortly'; cGMP-4 Phase 2 (~₹125 cr) operational by end Q4 FY27; MPP debottleneck commissioned Sep-2026 (a kept promise).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Promise-tracker prior: a project that has already slipped once has a materially higher chance of slipping again, even when the remaining window is short; partner-dependent qualification adds risk. Navin's other recent near-term promises were kept, which keeps us from going lower.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Indian chemical capex promised for the very next quarter is commissioned on time roughly 60% of the time.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if a Navin filing, press release, investor presentation or the Q3 FY27 earnings call states that the Chemours/advanced-cooling (two-phase immersion fluid) plant was commissioned (mechanically complete and started production) on or before 31-Dec-2026. 'Commissioning in Q4'/'in January' = NO.
- **Resolution source:** Navin Fluorine Q3 FY27 results presentation / earnings call transcript / NSE announcements
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/NAVINFLUOR_06112026142511_NFILIntimationofTranscriptofEarningsCallQ2FY27.pdf

**Visit C: customers and installers** (one DC facility/projects engineer or an EPC installer, one commercial-realty or hospital facility manager, one genset rental company)
10. **DC:** DG MW installed per IT MW (redundancy N+1 / 2N), genset brand split on the last 2–3 projects, the price per MW paid, and whether they were offered gas, BESS or fuel-cell alternatives. This resolves the §3.4 physics gap.
11. **Realty/hospital:** brand chosen and why (service reach, TCO, resale), running hours per year (standby utilisation drives parts intensity: the MD&A threat about a "low utilisation profile"), and whether rooftop solar plus BESS is replacing DG hours. Cummins' own BESS pilot is at the Phaltan MRC.
12. **Rental company:** fleet brand mix, utilisation and rental rates per kVA-month — a cyclical read on realty/infrastructure demand.

**Counts first, then opinions. Ethics:** identify yourself honestly if asked; do not solicit unpublished price-sensitive information; do not pay for information; no recordings without consent. Price quotes that a dealer would give any buyer are fair game.

**Output:** a price sheet by node and brand (the quarterly series), a lead-time table, a parts-price table, 5 quotes, and a "surprises vs model" list. Each of §3.1–4.5's estimates gets marked confirmed, contradicted or no read.
